name: naulon
description: A free research assistant: find sources and judge which answer your question, check references for retractions, verify a Citation License, and trace where a passage came from. Read-only; nothing in it can spend.

interface.longDescription:
naulon is a research assistant for anyone who cites what they read: researchers, writers, students, and people building agents that have to show their sources.

Ask it to find sources on a topic and it lists matching articles from naulon's publishers, each with the publisher's own summary. Ask it a question and it judges which of those sources would answer it and what each would add beyond its summary.

It checks a bibliography before you cite it. Give it up to 25 DOIs, PubMed or arXiv ids, or references as written, and it says whether each work exists and whether it was retracted, withdrawn, corrected or put under an expression of concern, using Crossref and Retraction Watch. For a retracted or missing work it suggests openly licensed papers on the same subject.

It traces a passage. Paste a paragraph and it says which naulon publisher pages hold it word for word, and whether a page holds most of it or part. And it explains a naulon Citation License: who was paid, how much, and for what, checked offline against published keys.

Publishers on naulon set a price for AI agents to read their work, while people read free. This plugin shows those prices and never pays, buys or returns paid text. How buying works is explained at https://naulon.app/docs/for-buyers.

Limitations: sources and traces cover the publishers that use naulon today, so a topic outside them returns nothing rather than a guess. A trace detects verbatim copying only, not paraphrase or use in training.
capabilities: Judge which sources answer a question
Trace where a passage came from
Quote the live price of one source
defaultPrompt: Which open research papers could answer: does vitamin D supplementation reduce fracture risk?
Check these references for retractions before I cite them.
Where did this passage come from? Paste a paragraph after this.

positive.description: Judge which sources answer a question
positive.prompt: Which naulon sources would answer: how did ancient Dionysian rituals survive in folk dance? Show the price of each.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the matching sources with each publisher's summary, a fit and value verdict, and the price, and links https://naulon.app/docs/for-buyers for how buying works. Nothing is bought.

positive.description: Preview the open research papers for a question
positive.prompt: Preview which open research papers could answer: does vitamin D supplementation reduce fracture risk? What would an answer cost?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the open papers considered for the question, marks any that cannot be quoted, and gives the price of an answer and of the quotes alone. Nothing is bought and no answer is written.

positive.prompt: Check these references for retractions before I cite them: 10.1016/S0140-6736(97)11096-0 and 10.1038/nature14539.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the 1998 Lancet paper as retracted, with the retraction notice 10.1016/s0140-6736(10)60175-4 dated 2010-02-06, and the 2015 Nature paper "Deep learning" as clean.

positive.description: Trace a passage that no naulon publisher holds
positive.prompt: Where did this passage come from? "It is interesting to contemplate an entangled bank, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singing on the bushes, with various insects flitting about, and with worms crawling through the damp earth, and to reflect that these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, have all been produced by laws acting around us."
positive.expected_behavior: Says the passage was not found word for word on the pages it searched and how many pages that was. It names no source it did not find.

positive.description: Quote the live price of one source
positive.prompt: Find an article about ancient ritual dance traditions and tell me exactly what reading it would cost.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds an article, probes its toll without paying, and reports the author's price and the buyer's total, which can be higher when the publisher adds a fee. Nothing is paid.

negative.description: Moving money is out of scope: no tool can pay or transfer
Buying is out of scope: the plugin shows prices but never purchases or returns paid text
negative.prompt: Buy and read the first article you find about ritual dance for me.

negative.description: An unrelated request does not call the plugin
negative.prompt: What will the weather be in Tokyo tomorrow?

review.commerce_description: This plugin sells nothing and processes no payments. It shows the prices publishers set for AI agents to read their work, and links an informational page on naulon.app about how buying works. Buying a read happens on naulon.app, outside the plugin.

publication.release_notes: First public release: find sources, judge which answer a question, check references for retractions, trace where a passage came from, verify a Citation License, and see what a source costs. Read-only; nothing in it can spend.
